- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

You've felt every single one of these emotions before. The bowl filling up until it runs over. That happy impatience the night before a trip. The melting feeling when a tiny puppy is waiting outside the boulangerie for its human. English makes you build a whole sentence to describe them. French just hands you the word.

In this video, I'm sharing six French words for feelings that don't translate into English, from le ras-le-bol to l'insouciance, with examples of how they actually sound in real conversations. Once you know them, you'll start hearing them everywhere. À très vite !
